title: Terms and Conditions
body:
CONDITIONS OF SALE
These Conditions of Sale set out the terms under which Sloane Street Auction Galleries Limited (“Sloane Street Auctions”) offers the lots listed in this catalogue
for sale. By registering to bid and/or by placing a bid at auction, you agree to be bound by these terms. You are strongly advised to read them carefully before participating in the auction.

Sloane Street Auctions acts as agent for the Seller. This means we provide services to assist the Seller in the sale of their lot, and that any contract of sale arising
from a successful bid is made directly between the Buyer and the Seller. Sloane Street Auctions is not a party to the contract of sale.

A. BEFORE THE SALE
1. Description of Lots
(a) Our descriptions of any lot in the catalogue, any condition reports, and any other statements made by us (whether orally or in writing), including about a lot’s
nature, condition, artist, period, materials, approximate dimensions, or provenance are our opinion. They should not be relied upon as statements of fact.
(b) We do not undertake in-depth research comparable to that carried out by professional historians or scholars. All dimensions, weights, and other physical
descriptions are approximate and provided for guidance only.
2. Condition
(a) All lots are sold ‘as is’, in the condition they are in at the time of sale, without any representation, warranty, or liability assumed by Sloane Street Auctions or
the Seller as to their condition.
(b) The condition of lots sold at our auctions can vary widely due to factors such as age, prior damage, restoration, repair, and general wear and tear. By nature, lots
are rarely in perfect condition.
(c) Any reference to condition in a catalogue entry or condition report does not constitute a complete condition report. Images may not show all aspects of a lot’s
condition, and colours or shades may differ in print or on screen from how they appear in person.
(d) Condition reports are provided free of charge for general guidance only and do not form part of the contract of sale. While we make reasonable efforts to
highlight notable issues, condition reports may not identify all faults, defects, restorations, or alterations. Our staff are not professional conservators or restorers,
and these reports are not a substitute for physical inspection or independent professional advice. It is your responsibility to request a condition report and to satisfy
yourself as to the lot’s condition.
Requests for condition reports must be submitted by 4:00 pm on the day before the auction.
3. Viewing Lots Pre-Auction
(a) If you intend to bid on a lot, you should inspect it personally or appoint a knowledgeable representative to do so. This is to ensure that you are fully satisfied
with the lot’s description and condition. We strongly recommend that you seek professional advice from a restorer or other professional adviser.
(b) Pre-auction viewings are open to the public free of charge. Our specialists may be available during scheduled viewing times or by appointment to provide
general guidance; however, such guidance does not constitute professional advice or a warranty of any kind.
4. Estimates
(a) Estimates are based on a lot’s condition, rarity, quality, provenance, and prices recently achieved for similar items. Estimates are prepared in advance of the sale
and may be amended by announcement before or during the auction. Estimates are in no sense definitive.
(b) The auctioneer may make a saleroom announcement before or during the auction that amends the lot’s description, estimate, or other material details. Estimates
should not be relied upon as an indication or guarantee of the lot’s final sale price or market value.
Estimates do not include the Buyer’s premium or applicable taxes.
5. Withdrawal of Lots
Sloane Street Auctions reserves the right to withdraw any lot at any time before or during the sale. We accept no liability for any decision to withdraw a lot or for
any consequences resulting from such a withdrawal.

B. REGISTERING TO BID
You must be over the age of 18 years old to register and bid with Sloane Street Auctions.
1. New Bidders
If this is your first time bidding at Sloane Street Auctions, you are strongly advised to register in advance of the auction to allow sufficient time for us to process
and approve your registration. We reserve the right, at our discretion, to decline to register you as a bidder.
You will be required to provide:
(i) A valid form of photo identification (such as a passport, national identity card, or driving licence); and
(ii) If not shown on the ID, proof of current address (e.g. a recent utility bill or bank statement).
(iii) We may request a deposit or impose bidding limits as a condition of registration, at our sole discretion.
2. Returning Bidders
We may, at our discretion, request up-to-date identification per paragraph B1 and may require a deposit as a condition of allowing you to bid.
3. Failure to Provide Required Documents
If, in our opinion, you do not satisfy our registration and identification requirements, including but not limited to compliance with antimoney laundering (AML),
we may refuse to register you to bid. If a successful bid has already been made, we reserve the right to cancel the resulting contract of sale at any time before
payment and collection.
4. Bidding on Behalf of Another Person
(a) Authorised bidder: If you are bidding on behalf of another person who will pay Sloane Street Auctions directly, that person must complete the registration
requirements outlined in paragraph B1. You must also provide a signed letter of authorisation from that person confirming you are permitted to bid on their behalf.
(b) Agent for a principal: If you register in your own name but are acting as agent for another party (the “ultimate buyer(s)”), you accept personal liability for the
purchase price and any other amounts due. You must disclose the identity of the ultimate Buyer (s), and we may require documentation to verify their identity.
5. Bidding in Person
If you wish to bid in person in the saleroom, you must register and obtain a numbered bidding paddle.
6. Bidding Services
(a) The following bidding services are offered free of charge as a convenience to clients. Sloane Street Auctions accepts no responsibility for any errors (human or
otherwise), omissions, or technical failures in the provision of these services:
(i) Telephone Bids: Requests to bid by telephone must be made at least one hour before the start of the auction. Telephone bidding is subject to staff
availability. If you require language support other than English, arrangements must be made in advance. Your use of this service is subject to these
Conditions of Sale.
(ii) Internet Bids: We accept online bids via Easy Live Auction, The Saleroom, and Invaluable. By bidding through any of these platforms, you agree to
be bound by our Conditions of Sale in addition to the terms of the relevant platform.
(iii) Absentee Bids: You may place an absentee bid using the form provided in this catalogue, or by contacting us. Confirmation of absentee bids will be
sent by email.
(b) Commission bids must be expressed in the saleroom’s currency and represent the maximum bid amount excluding Buyer’s premium. The auctioneer will use
reasonable efforts to execute absentee bids at the lowest possible price, subject to the reserve.
(c) In the event of two or more absentee bids at the same amount on a lot, and those are the highest bids, the lot will be sold to the bidder whose bid was received
first.

C. CONDUCTING THE SALE
1. Admission to the Auction
We reserve the absolute right to refuse admission to the premises or participation in the auction without stating a reason.
2. Reserves
Unless explicitly stated otherwise, all lots are subject to a reserve price, which will not exceed the lot’s low estimate. Lots offered without reserve will be marked
as “to be sold without reserve.”
3. Auctioneer’s Discretion
(a) The auctioneer has complete discretion and may, at any time:
(i) Refuse any bid;
(ii) Move the bidding forward or backwards in any manner;
(iii) Change the order of the lots;
(iv) Withdraw any lot;
(v) Divide or combine lots;
(vi) Reopen or continue the bidding even after the hammer has fallen; and
(vii) In the event of any error or dispute, whether during or after the auction, determine the successful bidder, cancel the sale of a lot, re-offer or
resell the lot, or take such other action as the auctioneer deems appropriate.
(b) If you believe the auctioneer has accepted a bid in error, you must submit a written notice detailing your claim within three business days of the auction. Sloane
Street Auctions will consider such claims in good faith.
(c) Nothing in this paragraph limits Sloane Street Auctions’ right to cancel a sale under any other applicable provisions of these Conditions of Sale.
4. Acceptable Bidding Methods
The auctioneer may accept bids from:
(i) Bidders present in the saleroom;
(ii) Telephone bidders;
(iii) Internet bidders; and
(iv) Absentee bidders who have placed bids with us before the auction.
5. Bidding on Behalf of the Seller
(a) The auctioneer may bid on behalf of the Seller up to, but not including, the reserve price. Such bids may be made consecutively or in response to other bids.
Seller bids made by the auctioneer will not be disclosed or identified during the sale.
(b) For lots offered without reserve, the auctioneer may open the bidding at approximately 50% of the lot’s low estimate. If no bid is received, the auctioneer may
lower the starting bid at their discretion until a bid is placed, then proceed upward. If no bids are received, the lot will be deemed unsold.
6. Bid Increments
Bidding will generally start below the low estimate and advance in increments determined solely by the auctioneer. The auctioneer retains full authority over the
opening bid and any subsequent increments.
7. Successful Bids
(a) Unless the auctioneer exercises discretion under paragraph C3 above, a legally binding contract for sale is formed when the auctioneer’s hammer falls on the
final bid.
(b) An invoice will be issued only to the registered bidder who placed the successful bid. While invoices will be sent by email after the sale, we accept no
responsibility for any failure to notify you of the outcome of your bid. If you believe you are the successful bidder but have not received an invoice, it is your
responsibility to contact us to confirm the result.
8. Compliance with Local Laws
By bidding in any sale, you agree to comply fully with all applicable local laws and regulations in force at the location of the auction.

D. THE BUYER’S PREMIUM, TAXES AND ARTIST’S RESALE ROYALTY
1. Buyer’s Premium
(a) In addition to the hammer price, the successful bidder agrees to pay a buyer’s premium on each lot sold. The Buyer’s premium will be charged as follows:
(i) 28% of the hammer price or;
(ii) 20% of the hammer price for wine, liquor and spirits.
(b) Value Added Tax (VAT) will be applied to the Buyer’s premium and is payable by the Buyer.
2. Taxes
(a) The successful bidder is responsible for all applicable taxes, including (but not limited to) VAT, sales tax, compensating use tax, or any equivalent tax, wherever
such taxes may arise, on both the hammer price and the Buyer’s premium.
(b) VAT charges and any potential refunds will depend on the Buyer’s individual circumstances. It is the Buyer’s responsibility to determine, report, and pay all
applicable taxes.
3. Artist’s Resale Royalty (ARR)
(a) In certain countries, local laws entitle the artist or the artist’s estate to a royalty, referred to as the Artist’s Resale Right, when works of art are resold. Lots
subject to Artist’s Resale Royalty are marked with the Δ symbol in the catalogue.
(b) Where applicable, the Buyer must pay an additional amount equal to the royalty due. Sloane Street Auctions will collect and remit such royalties to the relevant
collecting society or rights holder on behalf of the Seller.
(c) The artist’s resale royalty applies if the hammer price of the lot is £1,000 or more and is capped at £12,500 per lot. The royalty owed is as follows:
(i) 4% of the hammer price up to £50,000;
(ii) 3% of the hammer price between £50,000.01 and £200,000;
(iii) 1% of the hammer price between £200,000.01 and £350,000;
(iv) 0.5% of the hammer price between £350,000.01 and £500,000;
(v) 0.25% of the hammer price over £500,000, up to a maximum of £12,500 total royalty per lot.
(d) The artist’s resale royalty will be calculated using the euro to sterling exchange rate published by the European Central Bank on the date of the auction.
4. In Bond Wine Lots
(a) In bond lots, but available duty paid are marked with the W symbol in the catalogue
(i) If taken in bond, no VAT is charged on the hammer price. VAT will only be applied to the buyer’s
premium at standard rate.
(ii) If taken duty-paid, duty at the current rate, bond charges and the standard rate of VAT on the hammer price will be added to the hammer price.
(b) These lots are stored under bond and at the time of sale have not had UK Duty or VAT paid on them.
(e) Buyers of lots marked W may choose to have them transferred to their own bonded account, collected by a third party for shipment overseas or if they wish to
have the wines delivered, they must pay duty at the prevailing rate and VAT on the hammer price of the lot.

E. WARRANTIES
1. Seller’s Warranties
(a) The Seller is fully authorised to enter and perform its obligations under these Conditions of Sale
(b) The Seller warrants to Sloane Street Auctions and the Buyer that at all relevant times (including the time of the consignment of any item and the time of the
sale):
(i) The Seller is the sole and absolute owner of the property consigned, or is duly and properly authorised by the owner to sell it;
(ii) The Seller has, and shall transfer, good and marketable title to the Buyer free from any third‐party rights, claims, liens, charges, encumbrances, or
potential claims (including, without limitation, claims by governmental or regulatory authorities);
(iii) The Seller has provided Sloane Street Auctions in writing with complete, accurate, and not misleading information regarding: the property’s
provenance, authenticity, attribution, condition, and any restoration, repair, or alteration; the presence of any endangered or protected species materials
within the property; any concerns, disputes, or challenges, whether known to the Seller or raised by third parties, relating to the property’s ownership,
authenticity, attribution, condition, export, or import history;
(iv) Where the property has been imported into the United Kingdom, it was lawfully imported in compliance with all relevant laws, and all required
duties, taxes, and levies have been paid in full;
(v) The property is not subject to any export or import prohibition that would prevent its lawful sale, transfer, or shipment to the Buyer;
(vi) Unless the Seller advises Sloane Street Auctions in writing otherwise, before the delivery of the item, there are no restrictions on Sloane Street
Auctions’ rights to reproduce photographs or other images for any purpose related to the sale, marketing, or promotion of the lot;
(vii) Any electrical or mechanical goods or components are in safe operating condition. They are free from any defect not
apparent on external inspection that could present a danger to human life or health.
(c) The Seller shall fully indemnify Sloane Street Auctions and the Buyer against all claims, demands, proceedings, losses, liabilities, damages, costs, and expenses
(including legal fees) arising out of or in connection with:
(i) Any breach by the Seller of these warranties;
(ii) Any inaccuracy, omission, or misrepresentation by the Seller concerning the property;
(iii) Any failure by the Seller to comply with applicable laws, regulations, or requirements relating to the property.
(d) Where Sloane Street Auctions reasonably believes that there has been, or may be, a breach of any of the Seller’s warranties or representations, Sloane Street
Auctions may rescind the sale without liability.
(i) Should a breach of any of the Seller’s warranties or representations become apparent prior to the sale, the lot/s may be withdrawn and 20% + VAT of
the agreed reserve is payable by the Seller to Sloane Street Auctions within 30 days of the sale.
2. Buyer’s Warranties
(a) You represent and warrant that all funds used in connection with the purchase are lawfully obtained and not connected to criminal conduct, including but not
limited to fraud, money laundering, or tax evasion. You further warrant that you are not under investigation for, nor have you been charged with or convicted of,
money laundering, terrorist financing, or any other criminal offence.
(b) You agree to cooperate fully in providing documentation to support our anti-money laundering (AML) and know-your-customer (KYC) requirements,
including audit requests where necessary.
(c) If you are bidding as an agent on behalf of an ultimate buyer who will fund the purchase before you pay Sloane Street Auction Galleries, you further warrant
that:
(i) You have conducted appropriate customer due diligence on the ultimate Buyer (s) and complied with all applicable antimoney laundering, counter-
terrorist financing, and sanctions laws;
(ii) You will disclose the identity of the “ultimate buyer(s)” to us (including any officers, beneficial owners, or persons acting on their behalf) and, upon
request, provide documentation to verify their identity;
(iii) The arrangements between you and the “ultimate buyer(s)”, concerning the lot or otherwise, do not facilitate tax crimes in whole or in part; and
(iv) You have no knowledge or suspicion that the “ultimate buyer(s)”, their officers, beneficial owners, or any persons acting on their behalf, are on any
sanctions list, under investigation for, charged with, or convicted of money laundering, terrorist financing, or other crimes, or that the funds used are
linked to criminal proceeds, including tax evasion.

F. PAYMENT
1. How to Pay
(a) Immediately following the auction, you must pay the full purchase price, which comprises:
(i) The hammer price;
(ii) The Buyer’s premium;
(iii) Any amounts due under Section D3; and
(iv) Any applicable duties, sales, use, compensating, service tax or VAT.
(b) Payment is due no later than the end of the fourteenth calendar day after the date of the auction.
(c) We will only accept payment from the registered bidder. Once an invoice is issued, we are unable to change the Buyer’s name or reissue the invoice under a
different name. Payment is due immediately, even if you intend to export the lot or require an export licence.
(d) All payments for lots bought at Sloane Street Auctions in the United Kingdom must be made in the currency stated on the invoice and can be made using one
of the following methods:
(i) Wire Transfer: Payments should be made to Lloyd’s Bank, 98 Victoria Street, London, United Kingdom, SW1E 5JL Account Name: Sloane Street
Auction Galleries Limited. Account Number: 54140362 Sort Code: 30-98-97 BIC: LOYDGB21031 IBAN: GB52 LOYD 3098 9754 1403 62.
(ii) Credit Card: We accept most major credit cards, subject to certain conditions. Payments may be made in person or as a ‘cardholder not present’
(CNP) transaction by calling +44 (0)20 3915 8340. If your card is issued outside the UK, a cross-border transaction fee may apply. Please check with
your card provider before making a payment.
(iii) Cash: Cash payments may be accepted up to the legal limit permitted under applicable UK regulations. (vi) Cheque: Cheques must be drawn in
pounds sterling (GBP) and come from a UK bank account
(e) When making payment, please quote:
(i) The sale number;
(ii) The lot number(s);
(iii) Your full name.
2. Transfer of Ownership
You will not acquire title or legal ownership of any lot until complete and cleared payment of the entire purchase price has been received.
3. Transfer of Risk
Responsibility for and risk in the lot passes to you when the auctioneer’s hammer falls, and your bid is successful.
4. Consequences of Non-Payment
(a) If you fail to pay the full purchase price by the due date, we may exercise one or more of the following rights, in addition to any other legal remedies or the
rights set out below:
(i) Cancel the sale of the lot and resell it (publicly or privately) on terms we deem appropriate. If the resale results in a shortfall compared to your
original purchase price, you are liable to pay us the difference, including all resulting costs, expenses, legal fees, and any commission shortfall payable
to the Seller;
(ii) Initiate legal proceedings against you to recover the purchase price and associated costs (including interest, legal fees, and damages);
(iii) Offset your debts by deducting from any amounts we owe you (including any deposits or part-payments you’ve made);
(iv) Refuse bids made by or on behalf of you at future auctions or require a deposit from you before accepting further bids; (v) Take any other action we
deem necessary or appropriate.
(b) If you owe money to us, we may apply any payments you do make, whether deposits, part-payments, or funds otherwise due to you, towards satisfying any
outstanding balance.
5. Seller’s payment
(a) Net proceeds (after commission and other agreed-upon charges) will be paid to the Seller 35 calendar days following the auction, provided the Buyer has paid
in full and no dispute is pending.
(b) We charge a 2% + VAT loss and damage waiver, which will be deducted from the hammer price.

G. COLLECTION AND STORAGE
1. Collection Timeline
(a) You must collect any purchased lots within fourteen calendar days from the date of the auction.
(b) Please note that lots will not be released until we have received full and cleared payment of all amounts due, including the purchase price, Buyer’s premium,
and any applicable taxes or fees.
2. Uncollected Lots
If you do not collect your lot within fourteen calendar days after the auction, we may, at our discretion:
(i) Charge storage fees at a rate of £20 + VAT per lot from day 14, plus £5 + VAT per lot per additional day thereafter. Storage
charges will continue to accrue until the lot is collected and all outstanding balances are paid in full.
(ii) Sell the lot in any commercially reasonable manner and apply the proceeds toward any amounts owed to us, including storage
charges, resale costs, and administrative expenses.
3. Unsold Lots
Unsold lots must be collected within fourteen calendar days following the auction, unless they have been formally agreed in writing by
Sloane Street Auctions to be re-entered into a future sale. Where no such agreement exists, and the lot remains uncollected after this period, Sloane Street Auctions
may, at its sole discretion, impose storage charges, re-offer the lot for sale, or dispose of it in such manner as it deems appropriate.

H. TRANSPORT, SHIPPING, EXPORT AND IMPORT
1. Transport and Shipping
(a) You are responsible for making all necessary transport and shipping arrangements for any lots purchased.
(b) If requested, we can assist in arranging packing, transport, and shipping on your behalf, subject to your payment of all associated costs. However, we are not
professional packagers and do not accept any loss or damage once the item has left our premises.
(c) If you prefer, we may also suggest third-party handlers, packers, transporters, or experts. However, we disclaim all responsibility for third-party handlers,
regardless of whether they were recommended by us or chosen independently by you.
(d) Once the item has left our premises, we accept no liability for any loss or damage that may occur during handling, transport, or shipping.
2. Export and Import Restrictions
(a) The export and import of lots may be subject to laws, regulations, and restrictions in the country of sale or the country of destination.
(b) It is your sole responsibility to determine and comply with all legal requirements relating to the export from the country of sale and import into another country,
including but not limited to obtaining any export or import licences.
(c) If you are refused a licence or there is a delay in getting one, you must still pay us in full for the lot. We may be able to assist you in applying for the
appropriate licences, provided you request our assistance and pay our fee. However, we cannot guarantee that you will get one.
(d) Certain countries may prohibit the import of goods containing specific materials (e.g. ivory, endangered species, or cultural property). Buyers intending to
export any lot should ascertain:
(i) Whether an export licence is required from the country of sale; and
(ii) Whether any import prohibitions apply in the destination country.
(e) You are solely responsible for all applicable duties, taxes, tariffs, and government-imposed charges relating to the export or import of any lot.

I. OUR LIABILITY TO YOU
(a) Except as expressly stated in the Authenticity Warranty (see Section J) and to the extent permitted by law, we make no representation or warranty, express or
implied, regarding any statement or information provided by us, our employees, or representatives about any lot.
(b) All other warranties, terms, or conditions implied by law (including but not limited to satisfactory quality, merchantability, or fitness for purpose) are expressly
excluded.
(c) The warranties provided by the Seller under Section E1 are the Seller’s own. We do not accept any liability for those warranties.
1. Exclusions of Liability
We are not liable to you in connection with your purchase of or bid for any lot, or for any matter arising under these
Conditions of Sale, except:
(i) In the case of fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation by us, or
(ii) Where our liability is otherwise explicitly provided for in these Conditions of Sale.
2. No Guarantee of Lot Characteristics
We do not guarantee or accept liability for any lot concerning (whether stated or implied):
(i) Merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, or satisfactory quality;
(ii) Accuracy of description, size, condition, quality, or attribution;
(iii) Authenticity, provenance, rarity, importance, medium, literature, or exhibition history; or (iv) Any other aspect that might affect a lot’s value or
desirability.
3. Limit of Liability
If, despite the above exclusions, we are found to be liable to you for any reason, our liability shall not exceed the purchase price you paid to us for the relevant lot,
and we shall not be liable for any indirect or consequential losses, including but not limited to:
(i) Loss of profit or revenue;
(ii) Loss of opportunity;
(iii) Loss of anticipated savings or interest:
(iv) Business interruption; or
(v) Any other incidental or consequential damages or expenses.

J. OTHER TERMS
(a) We reserve the right to cancel the sale of a lot at our discretion if:
(i) Any of your warranties under Section E are found to be inaccurate or false;
(ii) We reasonably believe that completing the transaction would be unlawful or may become unlawful; or
(iii) We reasonably believe that proceeding with the sale could expose us or the Seller to liability or reputational harm.
(b) If any part of these Conditions of Sale is found by a court to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, that portion will be treated as deleted. The remainder of the
agreement will remain in full force and effect.
(c) You may not transfer, assign, or create a security interest over your rights or obligations under these Conditions of Sale without our prior written consent. These
Conditions are binding upon your estate, successors, and any party that acquires your rights or obligations.
(d) Any delay or failure by us to enforce a right or remedy under these Conditions shall not be considered a waiver of that right or remedy. Similarly, the partial or
single exercise of a right or remedy does not prevent further enforcement of that or any other right or remedy.
(e) By registering to bid, you agree to our use of your personal data under our Privacy Policy. This includes storing your data securely on our systems and
contacting you about the sale or other relevant auctions or services. You may request access to, or deletion of, your data at any time in accordance with applicable
data protection laws.
(f) These Conditions of Sale, and any contractual or non-contractual dispute arising out of or in connection with them, shall be governed by and construed in
accordance with English law and disputes shall be exclusively resolved in the English courts.
(g) We shall not be liable for any delay or failure to perform any obligations under these Conditions caused by events beyond our reasonable control, including but
not limited to natural disasters, strikes, governmental actions, or internet outages.
(h) These Conditions of Sale constitute the entire agreement between you and us concerning the subject matter and supersede any previous agreement,
understanding, or representation.
